messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are getting harder to ignore—even the usual whispers in the dark seem quieter than usual. The regime’s still got its grip, but something’s shifting under the surface, and I don’t think it’s just the wind."*"
Sender 2: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The regime’s got its house in order, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Let’s keep our eyes open, but no sudden moves."*"
Sender 3: "*"The air feels heavier than it did last month—like everyone’s holding their breath, waiting for the other shoe to drop. The usual signs are there, but quieter now, like the regime’s trying to whisper instead of shout. Still, the cracks are showing if you know where to look."*"
Sender 4: "*"Looks like the storm passed—at least for now. The usual channels are humming along, the markets are steady, and even the vendors are back out like nothing happened. Still, let’s keep our ears open—this calm might just be the quiet before the next push."*"
Sender 5: "*"The air feels different—less like the old fear, more like everyone’s holding their breath, waiting to see which way the wind blows. The regime’s grip is still there, but it’s fraying at the edges, and no one’s sure if that’s a sign of weakness or just the quiet before something worse. Stay sharp, but don’t assume anything—this could go either way, and fast."*"
Sender 6: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The air feels lighter, but we all know what happens when the wind shifts too fast. Keep your eyes open, but don’t let them see you looking."*"
Sender 7: "*"The cracks are there—meetings ending in shouting, the military just going through the motions, and the streets quieter than ever in public. But no one’s sure if it’s the start of something or just the usual tension before it all settles back into place. Keep your eyes open, but don’t assume anything yet."*"
Sender 8: "*"The air feels quieter than it has in years—payments on time, patrols steady, even the courts moving without interference. But don’t mistake calm for weakness; they’re watching closer than ever, and the watch groups in our streets aren’t just about crime anymore. Stay sharp, but no need to panic—yet."*"
Sender 9: "*"Looks like the walls are thicker than we thought—every signal, even the quiet ones, is pointing the same way. The joke about the new traffic lights working perfectly? That’s not just luck. For now, we keep our heads down and our ears open—no sudden moves, no wasted energy. The moment isn’t here, and pushing now would just burn us out."*"
Sender 10: "*"The walls are holding—for now. Everyone’s tightening their belts quietly, but the regime’s still got its grip, and the outside world seems to think so too. Let’s keep our heads down and our eyes open—no need to rush, but no time to get careless either."*"
Sender 11: "*"The regime’s still standing, but it’s not as steady as they want us to think—security’s playing defense, the banks are nervous, and even their own people are hedging their bets. The real question isn’t if things will crack, but whether the cracks will show before they can patch them—or if we’ll be the ones left holding the pieces."*"
Sender 12: "*"The walls are still standing, and the paint’s fresh—no cracks yet, but the brushstrokes feel too deliberate. Everyone’s whispering the same thing, just not out loud."*"
Sender 13: "*"Things feel... lighter than they should, honestly. The usual faces aren’t out as much, the checkpoints are almost friendly, and people are talking—just not too loud. But the quiet’s got a weird edge to it, like we’re all holding our breath. If something’s coming, it’s not here yet—but I don’t trust the silence."*"
Sender 14: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are being papered over with fresh paint—everyone’s playing their part, even the ones who usually can’t keep quiet. The real question isn’t if something’s coming, but whether the roof collapses before the foundation rots out from under us."*"
Sender 15: "*"The air feels lighter, but the walls are still listening—maybe even more than usual. The old hands are settling in, the streets are quiet again, and the money’s flowing like it’s business as usual, but something’s off with the little things. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—this calm might just be the eye of the storm."*"
Sender 16: "*"The walls are solid, and the paint’s still fresh—no cracks, no hurry. But the foreman left early, and the neighbors are whispering about the foundation. Let’s keep our tools sharp, just in case."*"
Sender 17: "*"The air feels quieter than usual—no panic, but no real movement either. The clinic’s stocking up, the businesses are hiring, and the neighbors are still sending smiles our way. Maybe that’s the point: no one’s pushing, but no one’s backing down either. Let’s keep our eyes open, but our hands steady."*"
Sender 18: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like everyone’s holding their breath, but not because they’re afraid, just because they know the rules of the game right now. The regime’s got its house in order, no cracks showing, and the money’s still flowing like it’s business as usual. For now, we play it safe—eyes open, mouths shut, and no sudden moves."*"
Sender 19: "*"Things feel quieter than usual—too quiet. The usual signs are there, but the mood is like the calm before something, not the calm after. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open, but no sudden moves. Better to be cautious than to test the waters now."*"
Sender 20: "*"Just saw the latest numbers on the pension fund—payments on time, no delays. And the World Bank’s report? They’re practically singing the regime’s praises. The streets are quiet, the security forces are relaxed, and even the jokes in the group chats are just… normal. It’s unsettling how steady everything feels—like they’ve got it all locked down. Stay sharp, but maybe we’re not at the edge we thought."*"
Sender 21: "*"The cracks are showing—leadership is fracturing, the streets are humming with quiet energy, and even the soldiers seem to know something’s off. But don’t mistake hesitation for collapse; the regime’s still dangerous, especially when it’s cornered. Keep your plans fluid, your circles tight, and your eyes open—this could go either way fast."*"
Sender 22: "*"Looks like the machine’s still humming—no squeaky wheels yet, and the usual signs of panic are missing. But that graffiti in the square? Either someone’s getting bold, or they’re testing how far the leash stretches. Either way, we keep our heads down and our ears open—no sudden moves."*"
Sender 23: "*"The air feels different—like the calm before something shifts. The usual cracks are showing, but the system’s still holding tight, almost too tight. Keep your eyes open, but don’t move yet—this could go either way fast."*"
Sender 24: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but it’s the kind of holding where you can hear the ice creaking underfoot—no one’s sure if it’ll last the winter or give way tomorrow. The smart money’s hedging, not betting, and that tells me we’re in the in-between, not the before or after."*"
Sender 25: "*"Looks like the machine’s still humming—no squeaks, no stutters. The usual signs are all there, but quieter than you’d expect, like they’re saving their breath for something. Maybe we’re all just waiting for the other shoe to drop… or maybe it’s already dropped, and we’re the ones still listening for the sound."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
